title: Xanthe and the Will
premise: Tamsin Almeida, archivist of St. Verrine's Cathedral, receives two anonymous letters about the same sealed will and locked crypt: one confessing to a decades-old forgery, the other promising a second confession if he can prove a witness — the testator's disinherited daughter — is still alive. As the inheritance trial looms, Tamsin discovers the cathedral's own provost engineered the forgery to seize the Almeida family estate, the same estate that once cast his own mother out. Following crypt ledgers and a gravedigger's silence, he finds the 'dead' witness living as the cathedral's night cleaner, and at the trial he chooses justice outside the law, presenting her testimony at the cost of his position — and gains the belonging he never had.
about_author: Zephyrine Brightwater is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing wills, deeds, and disputes in a northern cathedral city. Their fiction is known for quiet protagonists, ecclesiastical settings, and mysteries where the archives themselves become the crime scene.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Tamsin Almeida, meticulous cathedral archivist, receives two letters in the same handwriting: one confessing to forging a will sealed in the locked crypt, the other promising 'the rest' if he finds the witness everyone swears is dead. His POV establishes his pride in closing every case. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into compulsion as he realizes the letters name his own family's old estate.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Tamsin petitions the provost for access to the crypt where the original will is entombed with its testator, Edmund Vasse. The provost grants it too easily, and Tamsin notices fresh mortar on a vault that should be untouched. His POV; the beat is unease — the first sign the institution itself may be a player rather than a backdrop.

chapters.title: A Witness Sworn Dead
chapters.summary: Researching the Vasse estate dispute of thirty years ago, Tamsin learns the key witness — disinherited daughter Mirabel Vasse — was declared dead after a river drowning, no body recovered. He interviews the aging solicitor who probated the forged will and catches him lying about a detail only the forger would know. His POV; beat: the hunt becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Gravedigger's Silence
chapters.summary: Old Sexton Bram, who dug the Vasse grave, refuses to speak — until Tamsin notices the man flinches at the name Mirabel. That night someone ransacks the archive and steals the 1990s burial ledger. Tamsin's POV; emotional beat: fear, and the realization that his investigation is being mirrored by someone inside the cathedral.

chapters.title: What the Mortar Remembers
chapters.summary: Tamsin breaks into the crypt at night and finds the Vasse vault opened from inside the cathedral, its will replaced with a facsimile — but the facsimile is older than the confessed forgery, meaning there were two forgeries, generations apart. Interleaved with Mirabel's POV in fragments: she watches the cathedral lights and knows someone is digging. Beat: dread deepening on both sides.

chapters.title: The Confessor
chapters.summary: Tamsin traces the letters' paper to the cathedral gift shop and confronts the likely author: the dying former verger, who confesses he forged the will thirty years ago on the provost's orders — but insists Mirabel can prove the original terms. He gives Tamsin a key and dies before the trial date is set. His POV; beat: grief and urgency, the clock now audible.

chapters.title: Night Cleaner
chapters.summary: Following the key to a rented room behind the cathedral school, Tamsin finds Mirabel Vasse alive, working as the cathedral's night cleaner — hiding in plain sight for decades, protected by Bram. She distrusts him; he must admit the estate at stake once belonged to his own mother's family. Dual POV; beat: wary alliance, belonging offered and almost refused.

chapters.title: The Provost's Ledger
chapters.summary: The provost, exposed by the verger's death, offers Tamsin a bargain: silence and a promoted post, or ruin — he reveals he knows Tamsin's mother was turned away by the cathedral and that the estate's seizure funded the very archive Tamsin loves. Tamsin refuses. His POV; beat: the theme crystallizes — power corrupting the institution he served, and his choice to stand outside it.

chapters.title: The Trial Begins
chapters.summary: On the trial's first morning, the provost moves to have the will confirmed unopposed; the stolen ledger surfaces to brand Mirabel a fraud and a trespasser. Tamsin, barred as a witness due to his position, smuggles the verger's key and confession to Mirabel's counsel through the crypt's old ossuary passage. Alternating POV; beat: desperation, sacrifice, the law closing like a trap.

chapters.title: Testimony from the Dead
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution: Mirabel takes the stand as a woman legally dead, and her testimony — corroborated by the original will Tamsin recovered beneath the vault's false floor — unravels both forgeries. The provost is indicted; Tamsin resigns his post rather than preside over the cover-up's paperwork. In the final scene, he and Mirabel reopen the estate's garden gate together. Beat: justice outside the law, and belonging finally claimed.
